buttonLabel: "Learn more about festive journeys through Chile and Peru"
lead: >-
  The festive journeys featuring Chile and Peru in our selection begin with Carnival or New Year's Eve in Rio de Janeiro. Chile and Peru come later on a longer itinerary through five countries. Bolivia lies between them: after Santiago and the Atacama, travelers cross the Altiplano before reaching Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. The fixed date of the celebration and the actual sequence of transfers are therefore essential when choosing.
---

## Chile and Peru after Carnival: the order of the countries

Our themed selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. They all include Chile and Peru as **main countries** on the route, but the major celebrations take place **in Brazil**, at the beginning of the trip. This is not a calendar of festivals in Santiago and Cusco or a promise to attend celebrations in three countries at once.

These programs follow a common geographic sequence: Rio de Janeiro and Iguazú, Argentina, then [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), high-altitude Bolivia and the final days in Peru. **There is no direct uninterrupted Chile–Peru transfer that bypasses Bolivia.** Selecting the two countries identifies their overlap in a longer tour rather than a shortened stand-alone itinerary.

Compare other combinations on the [general Chile + Peru page](/multi-country/chile_peru/) and in [multi-country events and festivals tours](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/).

## Three trips: which celebration determines the calendar?

**[“Five Latin American Countries with the Champions' Parade in Rio: 18 Days”](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/)** is scheduled for **February 12–March 1, 2027**. The festive opening takes place in Rio, followed by Iguazú and Buenos Aires. In Chile, travelers discover Santiago, fly toward the Atacama and continue into Bolivia. Through Uyuni, La Paz and Titicaca, the route reaches Peru, including Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

**[“Carnival and the Best Sights of Five Countries in 19 Days”](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/)** is a private option. Carnival falls at the start of the Brazil section; Chile includes Santiago and the Atacama, and Peru concludes the journey after Bolivia. The itinerary features Puno, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Its key distinction is the individual format and a different schedule for city and high-altitude days.

**[“New Year's Tour of Five Countries in 19 Days”](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/)** is tied to the night of December 31 on Copacabana Beach. Chile follows in January, with Santiago and San Pedro de Atacama. The route then passes through Bolivia and the Uyuni Salt Flat before reaching Peru for Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

| Event | Itinerary |
|---|---|
| Champions' Parade | [18 days, group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) |
| Carnival | [19 days, private tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) |
| New Year's Eve | [19 days, group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) |

The three options have similar geography but different reasons for travel, formats and calendar dates. The Champions' Parade, other Carnival evenings and New Year's Eve are not interchangeable events.

## Chile: between the big celebration and the high-altitude road

After evening events and city tours in Brazil, the journey gradually shifts toward the Andes. Santiago includes a tour of its historic center and other city sightseeing. A flight to Calama then takes travelers to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Altitude, air dryness and road conditions change here, and the onward journey passes the high-altitude lagoons of Bolivia.

An important choice is how much time to spend in Chile. The Chilean section of these festive programs is relatively short and serves several purposes: introducing Santiago, changing climates and transitioning to the Altiplano. If you want an extended Atacama route with several days of excursions and observations, look at [themed tours including Chile](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/chile/) and their precise programs rather than assuming any festive journey has spare days.

**None of these three itineraries advertises a separate festival in Chile** comparable to the event in Rio. Geography and excursions take priority here. A ticket to an event in Brazil therefore does not automatically confirm any cultural program in Santiago.

## Between Chile and Peru: why Bolivia must be included in the calculation

After the Atacama, an extended off-road section begins through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). It then continues through La Paz and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) toward Lake Titicaca. Only after this does the group arrive in Peru.

This matters when choosing a trip in the Chile + Peru selection. The intervening country takes actual days and requires appropriate transport, accommodation and readiness for altitude. Travelers mainly interested in Santiago and Machu Picchu with a quick flight between them should understand that these festive routes **are not direct examples of that arrangement**.

To compare the Altiplano and Titicaca section specifically, explore the [Bolivia and Peru combination within festive journeys](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/events-and-festivals/). It describes the same extensive route from another geographic perspective, emphasizing Uyuni, La Paz and the crossing to Puno rather than Chile's Atacama.

## Peru: a cultural finale after the celebration dates

The Peruvian section of all three tours covers [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), travel to Cusco and a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), followed by the conclusion of the journey in Lima. It is a substantial cultural and historical program, not another city festival.

The sequence has one notable feature: Machu Picchu comes in the final part of a long journey. By then, travelers have already experienced the night-time event in Rio, international flights, the road to the Atacama, an off-road route across Bolivia and days at altitude near Titicaca. Anyone seeking more time in Peru should compare these days with [cultural routes in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). If the festive event is the priority, the question becomes whether the group can comfortably travel from Carnival or New Year's Eve to Machu Picchu.

No specific local Peruvian festivals or ceremonial celebrations are included in the described programs. An ordinary visit to a historic city should not be presented as attendance at an event.

## What to check before fixing the dates

For every festive trip, the date of the event in Brazil is established first. International and domestic flights, border crossings, high-altitude accommodation and access to Peruvian sites are then arranged around it. Decide in advance how important a particular evening at the Sambadrome or New Year's Eve on Copacabana is, and how much time to allow after returning late from the festivities.

We help coordinate the country sequence, ground transfers, city and nature excursions, and an appropriate pace at altitude. Entry rules, documents and medical limitations must be checked for the specific nationality, route and dates. Event tickets, archaeological-site availability and included services are confirmed for each tour individually.

## Frequently asked questions about festive tours through Chile and Peru

### Is there a direct transfer from Chile to Peru on these itineraries?

The described routes include **Bolivia** in between, with high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz. The selection therefore covers more countries than the filter names and requires time for the intervening section.

### Where does the main celebration take place?

In Brazil. The Carnival itineraries focus on Rio de Janeiro and the Sambadrome, while the New Year's itinerary celebrates on Copacabana. No separate compulsory festival in Chile or Peru is specified for these programs.

### Which is better: the group Champions' Parade or private Carnival?

Compare the exact festive evening, dates and accompanying services. The [18-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) is specifically dedicated to the Champions' Parade, while the [19-day private tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) is organized around Carnival. The post-Rio routes are similar, but these are different products.

### Can I spend more time in Peru instead of crossing Bolivia?

That requires a change to the original itinerary. Bolivia is a separate stage of the current festive options, and the Peruvian section begins after Titicaca. Reworking the sequence affects transport, duration and cost.

### Why discuss altitude before booking?

After coastal Rio and city sightseeing come the Atacama, Bolivia's Altiplano and the Peruvian Andes. Altitude and long transfers affect comfort and pace. Choose the route based on travelers' actual health and the tour's conditions, not simply the total number of countries.

lead: >-
  Chile and Peru play different gastronomic roles on our itineraries:
  Chile's Maipo Valley or VIK wineries, and lunches in Peru's Sacred Valley.
  Compare which tastings are included, which are optional and how to combine
  wine experiences with a journey through the Andes.
---

## Chile and Peru for wine and cuisine: how much of the trip focuses on food?

In [Chile](/chile/), travelers can visit a winery, see vineyards and learn about local wine production. In [Peru](/peru/), the focus is often different: Andean cuisine, regional produce and restaurants that form part of discovering the Inca Sacred Valley. The countries complement one another, but the exact experiences depend on the selected tour.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining both countries with the food and wine theme. **All also visit other countries**, most notably Bolivia. Gastronomy plays a different role in each. Two group itineraries offer an optional winery visit near Santiago. A longer private journey schedules a wine-focused day in Chile and dedicated food stops in Peru. Choose based on the actual days, not merely the theme label.

## Chile: Maipo Valley or VIK winery

### Maipo after exploring Santiago

The [20-day tour through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [12-day trip through Chile, Bolivia and Peru](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) include a sightseeing excursion in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). An optional [Maipo Valley wine excursion](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) with tasting can be added to this day.

Maipo Valley requires a separate trip from the city center. The winery visit should not automatically be treated as part of the included Santiago excursion: the schedule, content and additional payment must be agreed. If tasting is a top priority, it makes sense to allow adequate time for it before planning the flight to Calama and transfer toward the Atacama.

### VIK winery as a separate day

The [33-day luxury VIP journey through South America](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) is structured differently. After Peru and Bolivia, the route arrives in Chile, with a dedicated day at [VIK winery](/chile/place/vik-winery/). The itinerary includes a [helicopter journey, private tasting and lunch](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-helicopter-tasting-lunch/).

This arrangement calls for more coordination than an ordinary tasting near Santiago: the helicopter section depends on weather and operational conditions, and the winery visit follows a schedule. When comparing options, confirm the inclusions of the selected program and the conditions for changing individual stages.

## Peru: lunch as part of exploring the Sacred Valley

In the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), food naturally connects with archaeology, agricultural traditions and travel between settlements. However, an included breakfast or lunch on the road does not by itself turn a sightseeing day into a gastronomic tour.

The 33-day Ada Tours program provides two more specific examples. One day combines [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), [Maras](/peru/place/maras/) and [lunch at MIL Centro](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/moray-maras-mil-centro-lunch/). Another includes Pisac, Ollantaytambo and [lunch at Wayra](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/pisac-ollantaytambo-wayra-lunch/). These stops link cuisine to local geography rather than turning the trip into a string of unrelated restaurants.

The 12- and 20-day group programs concentrate their Peruvian stages on Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima. They include some lunches, but **separate visits to MIL Centro or Wayra are not specified**. It would be wrong to select these group tours expecting guaranteed fine dining.

## Three routes and the real role of gastronomy

| Program | Food and wine focus |
|---|---|
| [12 days: Chile, Bolivia, Peru](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) | Optional Maipo tasting; main route through Atacama and Uyuni |
| [20 days: six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Optional Maipo tasting; more cities and transfers |
| [33 days: extended VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) | VIK in Chile, MIL Centro and Wayra in Peru |

The first option suits travelers who want to see major Andean landscapes and add a wine tasting. The second offers a wider journey including Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, leaving less time specifically for gastronomy. The third has dedicated food and wine stages but requires considerably more vacation time and a larger budget.

To compare the full geography of tours through both countries, browse the [general Chile and Peru selection](/multi-country/chile_peru/). You can also explore [food and wine journeys in Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) and [food and wine journeys in Peru](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/peru/); those catalogs cover more than this particular intersection.

## Coordinating gastronomic days with the high-altitude route

Between Chilean Santiago and Peruvian cities, these itineraries pass through Bolivia: Altiplano lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz and the Titicaca area. Some days take place at elevations above 4,000 meters. A long road journey, early start or high-altitude overnight stay can affect travelers' well-being and leave little room for a relaxed gastronomic evening.

It is better to separate demanding high-altitude days from tastings. When choosing dates, Ada Tours helps arrange flights, overland sections and visits so that a wine day does not come immediately before an arduous early transfer. A restaurant day in Peru should also be linked to the overnight location instead of being inserted into any open space in the calendar.

The weather differs in Santiago, the Atacama, Cusco and high-altitude lagoons. Chilean vineyards, coastal Lima and the Altiplano's cold evenings call for different clothing. Comfortable shoes, layers, sun protection and a warm jacket for altitude are useful. If you want to visit a winery during agricultural operations, check that specific estate's calendar, not just the national season.

## Bookings, documents and expenses

A journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile requires a separate review of entry rules **for each traveler's nationality** and the border-crossing itinerary. Adding other countries increases the checks required. Permitted stays, transit rules and documents cannot be inferred from permission to enter just one of the countries.

The currencies are Peruvian soles, bolivianos and Chilean pesos. For tastings, restaurants and small purchases, find out beforehand which payment methods work with your cards, whether cash is accepted and what extra costs apply. Confirm separately whether the selected day includes transfers, admission, the tasting and lunch. Wine purchased in one country may be subject to customs restrictions on an international flight or overland border crossing.

## Frequently asked questions about food and wine tours in Chile and Peru

### Is a wine tasting included on every Chile and Peru tour?

No. On the [12-day group tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) and [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), visiting Maipo costs extra. The [33-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) has a dedicated day at VIK winery.

### Can Machu Picchu be combined with a Sacred Valley restaurant?

Yes, but it is best to schedule [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and restaurant visits on separate days. The 33-day tour includes lunches at MIL Centro and Wayra; the shorter group tours do not specify those restaurant experiences.

### Can I travel only through Chile and Peru without Bolivia?

Geographically yes, but the listed current Ada Tours food and wine programs include Bolivia on their main routes. A trip strictly limited to two countries would require a separately agreed option. A “Chile + Peru” filter does not mean all other countries are excluded.

### What matters most before paying?

Ask to see the specific tasting or restaurant day, its included services and surcharges. Then check the sequence of countries, altitudes, flights, documents and conditions for changing the itinerary.

targetPath: /multi-country/chile_peru/interests/nature/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Learn more about nature tours through Chile and Peru"
lead: >-
  Chile and Peru combine the Atacama Desert, the high Andes, Lake Titicaca and mountain valleys around Machu Picchu. But itineraries differ: some include nature excursions in the Atacama, while others visit mainly Santiago and Chile's coast. Compare the actual nature days, the route through Bolivia and the time allowed for acclimatization.
---

## Nature in Chile and Peru: what the route actually includes

Combining [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/) offers the chance to see the dry expanses of the Atacama and the much greener valleys of the eastern Andes. Bolivia's high-altitude regions often lie between them. The crucial question when choosing a trip is therefore **which natural attractions are scheduled and in which countries**, not simply whether Chile and Peru appear in the title.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The selection includes 12–14-day tours of Chile, Bolivia and Peru, as well as longer trips through several countries. Some include mainly city sightseeing in Chile. To explore all itineraries featuring these countries, visit the [Chile and Peru combination without the theme filter](/multi-country/chile_peru/).

## Where the Chilean nature experience begins

[San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) is a gateway to the desert and high-altitude scenery. Nearby are [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), salt flats, lagoons and the [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/). However, the attractions available throughout the region far outnumber those actually included in any individual tour.

The [12-day “Chile, Bolivia and Peru: Atacama, Uyuni, Machu Picchu” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) passes through San Pedro before continuing by jeep to Bolivia's lagoons and salt flats. The high-altitude lakes that travelers see next are **already in Bolivia**. A stop in San Pedro does not mean that Moon Valley or El Tatio is included automatically.

For comparison, the [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) focuses its Chilean section on Santiago, Valparaíso and Viña del Mar; it does not advertise a nature tour through the Atacama. It may suit travelers seeking nature experiences in other countries, but is not a substitute for a dedicated desert expedition.

## Peru: green valleys, Lake Titicaca and the mountains of Machu Picchu

The Peruvian stages often begin around Cusco. The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) combine history with steep mountain slopes and humid vegetation toward the eastern Andes. The archaeological complex is a historical and cultural landmark visited amid outstanding natural landscapes.

A very different environment is [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) near Puno. Its open highland scenery contrasts sharply with both the Atacama Desert and the valleys around Cusco. On the [14-day extended tour through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/), the itinerary starts with Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Titicaca, continues through Bolivia's Uyuni and Altiplano, and finishes at San Pedro and Santiago.

Travelers particularly interested in Peru's natural areas should compare [nature tours in Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) with [routes through Chile's natural regions](/interests/nature/tours/chile/). These help determine whether a long cross-border journey is appropriate or whether one region deserves more time.

## A third country is often the most important link

On itineraries through Bolivia, the cross-border nature sequence is Atacama and San Pedro → Bolivia's lagoons and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) → La Paz and the Titicaca area → Peruvian Cusco. This order, or its reverse, creates a substantial journey but takes time for roads, borders and changes in altitude.

The [VIP tour through Chile, Bolivia and Peru](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/) passes through Santiago, San Pedro, Uyuni, La Paz, Titicaca and Cusco. The VIP label describes the selection, but it does not automatically mean every transfer is private or every nature excursion includes special guiding. Check the exact travel arrangements and included services in the program.

On longer multi-country journeys, Chile may instead serve mainly as a stop in Santiago between distant flights. This is worthwhile for exploring the city but adds fewer nature experiences than several full days in the desert. Compare **not just the total duration but also time spent at natural attractions**.

## Choosing an itinerary

| Itinerary | Nature focus |
|---|---|
| Chile, Bolivia, Peru, 12 days | Atacama, lagoons, Andes |
| Peru, Bolivia, Chile, 14 days | Titicaca, Uyuni, Atacama |
| Four countries, 15 days | Iguazú and the Peruvian mountains |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_chile_bolivia_peru_group_12_days_2026,tour_source_velikij_tur_po_yuzhnoj_amerike,tour_source_vip_tur_v_peru,tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru}}

Begin with your main priority: volcanic scenery in the Atacama, Uyuni's salt flats or Peru's mountain valleys. If you want several days in the desert itself, look for them in the schedule. If Machu Picchu is the primary objective, review the duration and format of the visit, tickets and travel time from Cusco.

## Practicalities: altitude, site access and seasons

Cusco is at high altitude; La Paz and the Altiplano are higher still. Moving from low-lying cities to high-altitude overnight stays calls for time to acclimatize. Look at the sequence of stops and the actual overnight elevations, not just the highest elevation reached during an excursion. Good physical fitness does not guarantee protection from altitude sickness.

The Atacama can bring sunshine, dry air, cold mornings and windy highland areas. Around Cusco and Machu Picchu, the weather and walking conditions differ; humid slopes and rain make footwear just as important. Access to individual sectors of some natural areas in Chile may change with the weather, so current rules should be checked for the travel date.

Connections and overland crossings through Bolivia are particularly important. Check documents for **every** country on the actual route according to your nationality, along with insurance coverage and any need to book admission to protected sites in advance. The mere presence of Machu Picchu or the Atacama in a region does not imply access to any possible visitor route.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Chile and Peru

### Do all tours in this selection visit the Atacama Desert?

No. For example, the [15-day four-country program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) includes Santiago and the Chilean coast without an advertised trip into the Atacama. Compare the actual days of your chosen itinerary.

### Can I combine the Atacama and Machu Picchu in one journey?

Yes. The [12-day Chile, Bolivia and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) connects San Pedro, high-altitude Bolivia and Machu Picchu in Peru.

### Why is Bolivia included when I select Chile and Peru?

On several current itineraries, it provides the overland connection between natural areas. Bolivia adds lagoons and Uyuni, but also means another country, border procedures and high-altitude overnight stays.

### When is the best time to go?

There is no single ideal month for every region. Choose the main natural attraction and the dates for visiting it, then compare conditions in the other areas. The Atacama, Titicaca and Machu Picchu are affected by different weather factors.

lead: >-
  A 33-day journey through Peru and Chile includes a boat trip to the Ballestas Islands,
  a cruise in the Peruvian Amazon and a visit to the Puñihuil penguin colony when weather permits.
  These differ from trips focusing on deserts, lagoons and mountain panoramas.
  Compare the included wildlife experiences, seasonal conditions and landscape-focused alternatives.

## Wildlife watching in Chile and Peru: which excursions are included?

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Chile and Peru among the main countries and the “Wildlife and Safaris” theme. The 33-day itinerary confirms the Ballestas Islands, the Peruvian Amazon and Puñihuil in Chile when the weather is favorable. **Lagoons, waterfalls and historic complexes do not, by themselves, mean dedicated wildlife watching.** We also consider landscape-focused alternatives that fall under the Nature theme.

In [Peru](/peru/), many itineraries lead from [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). In [Chile](/chile/), popular destinations include [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and high-altitude lagoons, while longer routes reach Patagonia. Scenic views, walks around historic sites and wildlife watching are different activities, each requiring its own time.

## What each country offers nature lovers

| Region | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Paracas, Peru | Seabirds and sea lions |
| Titicaca, Peru | Lake and highlands |
| Atacama, Chile | Lagoons and flamingos |
| Chiloé, Chile | Coastal birds |
| Patagonia, Chile | Lakes, glaciers, mountains |

**Peru's coast.** The [33-day extended journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) includes a boat trip to the Ballestas Islands from the [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/) area. Sea lions, seabirds and Humboldt penguins inhabit these islands. The marine excursion is an actual part of this tour, although departure and viewing conditions depend on the sea and protected-area regulations. Tours devoted solely to Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley do not automatically include it.

**Highland Peru.** [Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) introduce travelers to the high-altitude lake and the life of local communities. The landscape matters more here than any promise to see a specific animal species. Birdwatching would require a suitable location and time to be planned separately rather than assumed from the word “nature” in the selection title.

**Northern Chile.** [Los Flamencos National Reserve](/chile/place/los-flamencos-national-reserve/) comprises natural areas around the Atacama, including salt flats and high-altitude lagoons. They provide flamingo habitat, but visiting the [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) or Moon Valley does not guarantee sightings. The exact sector, permitted visiting time and access conditions matter.

**Southern Chile.** Longer tours may travel through [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) and the lake district to Chiloé Island. The 33-day itinerary mentions the [Puñihuil penguin colony](/chile/place/punihuil-penguin-colony/), **weather permitting**. That distinguishes it from a short journey limited to Santiago and the Atacama, which does not reach the south.

## Which programs suit different nature-related goals?

The table below compares programs with included opportunities to watch wild animals or birds. Scenic routes without such activities can be explored in the [nature travel selection](/multi-country/chile_peru/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife watching may take place outside the countries named in a selection; check the full route and exact days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_luxury_33_days}}

A landscape-focused alternative outside this wildlife selection is the [VIP trip through Chile, Bolivia and Peru](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/). It connects the Atacama, Bolivia's Uyuni Salt Flat, lagoons and the Peruvian Andes. Its strength is the succession of very different landscapes; an excursion to Peru's ocean islands is not included.

Another scenic alternative without the wildlife theme is the [14-day tour through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/). It includes Titicaca, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), colorful lagoons and the Atacama. This is primarily a high-altitude journey with long transfers. Travelers seeking particular bird species, not just landscapes, should check which stops are actually devoted to observation.

The [33-day extended itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) features the Peruvian Amazon and Paracas, followed by Bolivia, Chile, Easter Island and Patagonia. Marine wildlife areas and Puñihuil are genuinely included alongside many cultural and transport stages. The trade-off is time: the format suits travelers who want several ecosystems and are comfortable with complex logistics.

Some other tours in the general catalog fall under the Nature theme because they include [Iguazú in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) or lagoons in Bolivia. These are valuable stops but **do not become wildlife watching in Chile and Peru**. For a more focused geography, compare [wildlife tours in Peru](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/) and [wildlife tours in Chile](/interests/wildlife/tours/chile/).

## Why Chile and Peru are often connected through Bolivia

The two selected countries are often stages of a longer route. After Titicaca in Peru, travelers cross Bolivia via [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the [Laguna Colorada area](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), before reaching Chile's Atacama. This shows more natural regions but adds borders, high-altitude overnight stays and days in a vehicle.

The content of these days matters to nature lovers. If your main goal is unhurried birdwatching at a lagoon, a busy jeep route does not replace a stop at the appropriate time. If the combination of desert, mountain lakes and salt flats matters more, the Altiplano may become the highlight of the trip. We help organize the sequence of stops and decide how much time to allocate to nature activities. The exact itinerary must be agreed before booking.

## Altitude, seasons, clothing and visiting rules

The journey connects the Pacific coast with the high Andes. After Lima, travelers may quickly reach Cusco and then the Bolivian Altiplano. The rate of ascent and overnight elevation matter; even excellent fitness does not prevent altitude sickness. A sensible route sequence and acclimatization time are necessary. Travelers with chronic illness or individual risks should discuss the trip with a doctor in advance.

Ocean excursions near Paracas depend on sea conditions. Atacama lagoon visits are subject to current access restrictions in [Los Flamencos](/chile/place/los-flamencos-national-reserve/) and instructions from local guides. In southern Chile, allow for wind and changing weather; in [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), stay on marked trails and do not approach animals for a photograph.

Pack in layers: sun protection, warm clothes for high-altitude mornings, a windproof jacket and shoes suitable for designated routes. Travel documents must be checked for nationality and the **complete** set of countries, including Bolivia if it is on the itinerary. When entering Chile, comply with declaration rules for plant and animal products, including at land borders. Confirm payment methods and currencies in each country: carrying US dollars does not mean they will be accepted everywhere.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Chile and Peru

### Can I see flamingos in Chile on every tour?

No. The route must include a suitable lagoon area and time for observation. Some trips are limited to Atacama panoramas, and birdwatching may not be included at all.

### Do Peru itineraries include marine animals?

Yes, some longer tours visit the Ballestas Islands near [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/). Most routes through Cusco and Machu Picchu focus on other attractions, so a marine excursion must be checked separately.

### Do I have to add Bolivia?

No, but many existing itineraries connect Chile and Peru through Bolivia. Compare the complete route, number of borders and overnight elevations rather than just the two countries in the filter.

### Which option is best for photographing animals?

Choose an itinerary that includes a **wildlife-watching excursion** and time for photography, such as the Ballestas Islands, an appropriate Atacama lagoon sector or Puñihuil. The broader [multi-country wildlife tour selection](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) helps compare options.

## Chile, Peru and Uruguay: how these countries connect on current tours

**Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through all three countries on the main route.** This is a geographic overlap, not a promise of a separate tour limited to Chile, Peru and Uruguay. The actual itineraries pass through other South American countries, and their order matters.

[“Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days”](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) combines Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) itinerary adds Ecuador and Colombia, including the Galápagos Islands. Both first take travelers via Buenos Aires to Montevideo, then continue into Chile and reach Peru only after crossing Bolivia's highlands.

It is also worth comparing the [general catalog of multi-country itineraries](/multi-country/): if you have only 10–12 days, visiting two neighboring countries can sometimes leave more time for sights and less time in the air.

## Uruguay: Montevideo on a day trip from Buenos Aires

On both itineraries, Uruguay primarily means [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). After an early transfer to the port, travelers take a ferry from Buenos Aires, spend the day sightseeing and return to Argentina. This is a specific excursion, not several beach days in Punta del Este or a direct onward journey from Uruguay to Chile.

Montevideo's program includes the historic center, city squares and the port area. Travelers wanting a deeper introduction to the country should compare [places in Uruguay](/uruguay/place/) with those actually included on these multi-country tours.

**The main organizational issue is the ferry and re-entry into Argentina.** Border formalities apply in both directions even if you continue staying in Buenos Aires. You need valid documents, passenger details matching the tickets, sufficient time before boarding and a plan for your main luggage. Taking only essentials is generally more convenient for a short day trip, but the operator sets baggage rules.

Do not arrange a separate international evening flight on the same day without checking ferry timetables and ground transfers. On the current itineraries, the flight from Buenos Aires to Santiago comes at the next stage, after the Uruguay excursion.

## Chile: from Santiago to the Atacama Desert

The Chilean section starts in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A sightseeing tour introduces the historic center; on one program, a winery trip to the Maipo Valley can be added separately. The proximity of vineyards to the capital does not mean a tasting is included for every traveler.

The route then goes by air to Calama and by road to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stop also helps travelers acclimatize before the next, higher-altitude stage. An astronomy excursion is listed as optional, subject to observation conditions and confirmation at booking.

From San Pedro, travelers head to the Bolivian border and switch to off-road vehicles for a route through high-altitude lagoons to Uyuni. Although this selection is titled Chile, Peru and Uruguay, **Bolivia is the country that connects the Chilean and Peruvian stages** on both current tours. A direct Santiago–Cusco transfer cannot be assumed.

Weather in early November varies considerably: Santiago is in spring, the desert may be intensely sunny by day, and mornings and nights on high-altitude roads can be much colder. Pack light daytime clothing, a warm layer and protection from wind and sun. The [Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/) describes other possibilities.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu after the Altiplano

The Peruvian section does not begin in Lima. After the Bolivian stops, travelers pass Tiwanaku and the Desaguadero border area to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Next comes an Andean road journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

Altitude is the main concern on this section. The body will already have spent time on the plateau after the Atacama and Bolivian lagoons, but this does not guarantee protection from altitude sickness. Consider overnight elevations, overall well-being and recovery time. Travelers with chronic illness, particularly cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, should discuss the route with a doctor beforehand.

**Entry to Machu Picchu is tied to a specific ticket, date, time and visitor circuit.** Peru's Ministry of Culture operates an official booking system with a selection of routes. Changing the departure day from Cusco on the assumption that any ticket can be purchased on arrival is therefore risky. The current Ada Tours itineraries include a guided visit and train ticket, but exact services must be checked for the chosen tour.

Late October and November mark a transition toward the wetter season in the Peruvian Andes. A brief downpour may affect walks and trail conditions even when the morning is sunny. A rain jacket, sturdy footwear and a small daypack are more useful than one all-purpose outfit for “hot South America.”

## How much time and travel are actually needed?

The sequence **Buenos Aires → Montevideo → Buenos Aires → Santiago → Calama → San Pedro de Atacama → Bolivia → Puno → Cusco → Lima** shows why these three countries should not be treated as a nearby group. Between Uruguay and Chile is an international flight from Argentina; between Chile and Peru is an off-road high-altitude journey through Bolivia.

The 20-day itinerary lists dates of October 23–November 11, 2026. The 32-day tour lists October 22–November 22, 2026, and continues from Lima to Ecuador and Colombia. These are specific departures, not confirmation of future dates. Current availability and changes to the stop sequence are agreed at booking.

What to check for each transport stage:

- **Ferry to Montevideo:** documents for leaving and re-entering Argentina, baggage and time at the port.
- **International flight to Santiago:** the exact Buenos Aires departure airport, check-in time and ticket conditions.
- **Calama–Atacama–Bolivian border:** local transport, early departures, altitude and more basic accommodation on expedition nights.
- **Bolivia–Peru:** border control, followed by long road journeys through the Andes and a pre-booked entry time for Machu Picchu.

We help coordinate tickets, sightseeing order and border-crossing times with the selected itinerary, keeping the long journey feasible without artificially compressing days.

For travelers holding ordinary Russian international passports, published official lists indicate that **Peru and Uruguay allow short tourist visits without a visa obtained in advance**. Chile has a temporary tourist stay category normally lasting up to 90 days, but advance authorization requirements depend on nationality and the grounds for entry. Other nationalities may face different rules.

These checks cover only the countries named in the selection. **Both actual tours also visit Brazil, Argentina and Bolivia**, and the 32-day trip adds Ecuador and Colombia. List every entry and transit airport, including re-entry into Argentina after the ferry. Passport validity, children's documents, onward tickets and migration requirements must be checked for the entire route, not one catalog title.

## Frequently asked questions about travel through Chile, Peru and Uruguay

### Can I visit only these three countries on either tour?

Both current programs include other countries. The 20-day route also visits Brazil, Argentina and Bolivia; the 32-day route adds Ecuador and Colombia. If you want exactly three countries, the sequence and separate travel product must be arranged individually.

### Is there an overnight stay in Uruguay?

On both listed itineraries, Montevideo is visited on a day trip from Buenos Aires with a ferry return. Several days in Uruguay are not specified.

### Do travelers go directly from Chile to Peru?

No. After the [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the Bolivian section passes [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and La Paz, before crossing into Peru near Desaguadero. Time in Bolivia is a substantial part of the route.

### When should Machu Picchu be scheduled?

First agree a specific date and an available visitor circuit, then coordinate tickets and travel through Cusco. Andean weather varies, and entry to the monument is assigned to a time slot. Explore more options in the [Peru tour catalog](/peru/tour/).

### Can I manage this itinerary without specialized physical training?

The program combines city sightseeing and transport with high-altitude days. Sitting comfortably in a vehicle does not remove the risk of altitude effects. If unsure about your tolerance of the plateau, discuss elevations and overnight stays with your doctor and the organizer in advance.
